title: Seven selected dusty dwarfs show no resolved NEOWISE centroid response after local corrections
abstract: We test whether variable infrared emission can be located on seven field-kinematics dust candidates. A new reduction of NEOWISE 2014-2024 positions gives 149 target visits. We use 3-45 local reference groups per field, seasonal offsets and a linear time term. No target has a resolved inverse-flux centroid response at a seven-target threshold under the tested error models. With a 0.05 arcsec visit floor, conditional simultaneous response envelopes span 0.605-6.347 arcsec; a temporal covariance envelope widens them to 0.955-10.686 arcsec. We also show that the exact response of an ideal two-source photocentre is separation times constant-source flux fraction. Thus a small flux-linked shift alone is not a source-separation bound. This corrects a prior slope interpretation without showing that its candidates are blends. Limits include assumed errors, few references in some fields, measured-flux errors, prior selection and multiband position fitting. We infer no source separation, dust species or new event. Code, query hashes, original inference results and external-scratch retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Conditional centroid-response envelopes for seven selected candidates, and the exact dilution relation for an ideal two-source photocentre. The envelopes are not source-separation bounds.
